h1:
Korat Noodles & Mee Takhu
10 Spots the Locals Actually Eat At
intro: Korat is a serious noodle town. You'll find everything from decades-old clear-broth beef noodle shops to Ayutthaya-style boat noodles, plus Korat pad mee made with the original Mee Takhu noodles from Pak Thong Chai. We've picked 10 spots that locals genuinely line up for, with the area, prices and best time to go for each.

blocks.html: When people think of Korat food, pad mee usually comes to mind first — but this is a city that takes its noodle soup just as seriously, especially clear-broth beef noodles, with old-school shops scattered all over town. Some have been going 30 years or more: the broth looks clear but tastes deeply of beef, so you barely need to season it. We've split things into two main camps — noodle soup and boat noodles on one side, pad mee takhu on the other — then ranked them out for you.

items.name: Hom Ocha (opposite the Shell station)
items.blurb: A clear-broth beef ball noodle shop that's been part of Korat for years. The beef balls are house-made, the beef is fresh and tender, and the broth is clear but rich enough that you don't need to season it. Locals rank this among the very best for beef noodles.
items.meta: Beef & pork noodles · opposite the Shell station

items.name: Korat Beef Noodles (Phutthamonthon Sai 1)
items.blurb: A roadside beef noodle shop on Phutthamonthon Sai 1, known for piling the bowl high with both braised and fresh beef. The broth is fragrant with spices, and it pairs well with the bouncy beef balls. A common stop for drivers passing through.

items.name: Por Prateep Boat Noodles (SUT Gate 1)
items.blurb: Traditional Ayutthaya-style boat noodles with a rich, well-balanced broth. The small bowls are very cheap, so it's easy to order several at once — great for SUT students and anyone who likes that thick, concentrated broth.

items.name: Pad Mee Pa Yuan (Pak Thong Chai)
items.blurb: An old-school Korat pad mee shop in Pak Thong Chai district, the home of original Mee Takhu noodles. It's been going more than 40 years, with a balanced flavour that leans sweet. Eat it with fried chicken wings and drumsticks — well worth a stop if you're passing through Pak Thong Chai.
items.meta: Pad mee takhu · Pak Thong Chai district

items.name: Je Noi Krathok
items.blurb: A pad mee and made-to-order shop that gets a lot of love from Korat locals. The flavours are bold and well-seasoned, and the noodles stay chewy without going mushy. Reliably packed at lunchtime.
items.meta: Pad mee & made-to-order · in Korat city

items.name: Pad Mee Yai Ruam Ta Chuay (next to Wat Lak Roi)
items.blurb: A pad mee shop in the lane beside Wat Lak Roi on Mukkhamontri Rd. It's been open more than 10 years, cooked fresh one plate at a time, with orders piling up at lunch. A regular spot for people who work nearby.

items.name: Pa Aom Pad Mee on Banana Leaf
items.blurb: Korat pad mee served on a banana leaf, the leaf's aroma playing off the sweet-leaning noodles. The 60-baht special comes with fresh veg, and the shop gets good reviews for cleanliness and homemade flavour.
items.meta: Banana-leaf pad mee · in Korat city

items.name: Ko Liang Beef Noodles
items.blurb: Clear-broth beef noodles loaded with toppings — braised beef, fresh beef and beef balls. The broth is easy-drinking and doesn't need much seasoning. Another beef noodle shop locals keep coming back to.

items.name: Ko Seng Boat Noodles (Pandin Thong 7)
items.blurb: Thick-broth boat noodles in the Pandin Thong area. Cheap enough to order several bowls without hurting your wallet, with generous offal and beef balls. Great for anyone who likes traditional-style boat noodles.

items.name: Por Po Tom Yum Noodles with Bouncy Pork
items.blurb: Tom yum noodles packed with toppings and bouncy pork made fresh every day, with a sour-spicy tom yum broth that really lands. For people who like their noodle soup bold and tangy rather than clear.
items.meta: Tom yum noodles · in Korat city

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Many old-school pad mee and beef noodle shops sell out fast, especially the ones that only open morning to midday. If you want to hit a famous spot without disappointment, get there before 1pm to be safe — and quite a few are cash only, so bring small notes.

blocks.text: Korat Pad Mee vs Mee Takhu — What's the Difference?

blocks.html: People often mix up "Korat pad mee" and "Mee Takhu." Mee Takhu is actually the noodle itself, made in Takhu sub-district, Pak Thong Chai — a chewy rice vermicelli that's been sun-dried the same way for generations. Korat pad mee is the dish: those Mee Takhu noodles (or regular Korat noodles) stir-fried in a special sauce that leans sweet, then sour and salty, with egg and garlic chives, served with bean sprouts and lime.

items: Mee Takhu — the original dried noodle from Takhu sub-district, Pak Thong Chai. Buy a pack to take home and stir-fry yourself.
Korat pad mee — the dish of noodles stir-fried in a special sweet-leaning sauce, a local everyday staple.
Take the noodles home as a souvenir — sold both as plain dried noodles and as kits with ready-made sauce, so they're easy to cook at home.

blocks.text: Pick by the Style You're Into

items.name: Clear-broth camp
items.blurb: Craving clear, beefy beef noodles? Start with Hom Ocha or Korat Beef Noodles on Phutthamonthon Sai 1.

items.name: Pad mee camp
items.blurb: Want to try the city's signature dish? Head to Pad Mee Pa Yuan in Pak Thong Chai, or Je Noi Krathok in town.

items.name: Budget camp
items.blurb: Want lots of bowls on a small budget? Boat noodles at Por Prateep or Ko Seng start at 15–20 THB a bowl.

faq.q: Which shop has the best Korat pad mee?
faq.a: The most-reviewed spots are Pad Mee Pa Yuan in Pak Thong Chai (going more than 40 years, in the home of Mee Takhu noodles), Je Noi Krathok in town, and Pad Mee Yai Ruam Ta Chuay next to Wat Lak Roi. Most plates run 40–70 THB. Go around lunch, since it's cooked fresh one plate at a time.

faq.q: What is Mee Takhu and how is it different from Korat pad mee?
faq.a: Mee Takhu is the original dried noodle from Takhu sub-district, Pak Thong Chai district. Korat pad mee is the dish that takes those noodles and stir-fries them in a special sauce. Put simply: Mee Takhu is the noodle, Korat pad mee is the plate of food.

faq.q: Which shop has the best beef noodles in Korat?
faq.a: Hom Ocha (opposite the Shell station) does clear-broth beef noodles with house-made beef balls and is rated among the very best. The roadside beef noodle shop on Phutthamonthon Sai 1 is also known for piling the bowl high with braised and fresh beef.

faq.q: How much do noodles cost in Korat?
faq.a: Boat noodles start at 15–25 THB a bowl, beef noodles and tom yum noodles run 45–70 THB a bowl, and Korat pad mee is 40–70 THB a plate — cheaper than in many bigger cities.

faq.q: How late do noodle shops in Korat stay open?
faq.a: Many old-school beef noodle and pad mee shops open morning to midday and sell out fast, so go before 1pm. Some boat noodle and tom yum shops stay open into the evening — check the shop's Facebook page before you go.
